title: Sudden CEO death and firm value

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
- Method: Event Study. For each firm experiencing a sudden CEO death, estimate a market model in the pre-event estimation window [−10, −2], compute abnormal returns (AR) as residuals from that model, and test whether the cross-sectional mean cumulative abnormal return (CAR) over the event window [0, +1] is significantly different from zero.
- Why: Sudden CEO deaths are plausibly exogenous, discrete shocks to firm leadership. An event study isolates the immediate stock-price reaction, attributing deviations from normal returns to the event.
- Key assumptions:
  - Exogeneity/no confounding: The CEO deaths are unexpected and not systematically coincident with other firm-specific news within [0, +1].
  - Market efficiency/semi-strong form: Prices incorporate news quickly, so the effect loads into [0, +1].
  - Correctly specified normal-return model: The pre-event market model parameters are stable and valid for the immediate post-event window.
  - Cross-sectional independence (or weak dependence): For inference using t-tests across firms.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Complete, self-contained R code that:
# - Reads the CSV file from the path provided
# - Runs the appropriate causal analysis
# - Prints a clear numerical result (coefficient, CAR, etc.)
# - Includes basic robustness checks

# Load data
df <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s12_data.csv")
df <- df[order(df$stock_id, df$event_day), ]

# 1) Estimate the market model per firm using estimation window [-10, -2]
est <- df[df$event_day >= -10 & df$event_day <= -2, ]

uids <- sort(unique(est$stock_id))
coef_df <- data.frame(stock_id=integer(), alpha_hat=double(), beta_hat=double(), 
                      stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

for (id in uids) {
  d <- est[est$stock_id == id, ]
  d <- d[is.finite(d$ret) & is.finite(d$mkt_ret), ]
  if (nrow(d) >= 3) {
    fit <- lm(ret ~ mkt_ret, data = d)
    co <- coef(fit)
    alpha_hat <- unname(co["(Intercept)"])
    beta_hat  <- unname(co["mkt_ret"])
  } else {
    alpha_hat <- NA_real_
    beta_hat  <- NA_real_
  }
  coef_df <- rbind(coef_df, data.frame(stock_id = id, alpha_hat = alpha_hat, beta_hat = beta_hat))
}

# 2) Compute abnormal returns (market model) and CAR over [0, +1]
df2 <- merge(df, coef_df, by = "stock_id", all.x = TRUE)
df2$exp_ret_mm <- df2$alpha_hat + df2$beta_hat * df2$mkt_ret
df2$ar_mm <- df2$ret - df2$exp_ret_mm

# Event window [0, +1]
ev <- df2[df2$event_day %in% c(0, 1), ]

# CAR per firm
car_mm <- aggregate(ar_mm ~ stock_id, data = ev, sum, na.rm = TRUE)
names(car_mm)[2] <- "CAR_mm"
car_mm <- car_mm[is.finite(car_mm$CAR_mm), ]

# Main test: mean CAR significantly different from 0?
n <- nrow(car_mm)
meanCAR <- mean(car_mm$CAR_mm)
sdCAR <- sd(car_mm$CAR_mm)
se <- sdCAR / sqrt(n)
tstat <- ifelse(se > 0, meanCAR / se, NA_real_)
pval <- ifelse(is.finite(tstat), 2 * pt(-abs(tstat), df = n - 1), NA_real_)

cat("Main result: Mean CAR[0,+1] (market model) =",
    round(100 * meanCAR, 3), "%; t =", round(tstat, 3),
    "; p-value =", signif(pval, 3), "; N firms =", n, "\n")

# Also report AARs on day 0 and +1
aar0 <- ev[ev$event_day == 0, c("stock_id", "ar_mm")]
aar1 <- ev[ev$event_day == 1, c("stock_id", "ar_mm")]

m0 <- mean(aar0$ar_mm, na.rm = TRUE); s0 <- sd(aar0$ar_mm, na.rm = TRUE); n0 <- sum(is.finite(aar0$ar_mm))
t0 <- ifelse(n0 > 1 && s0 > 0, m0 / (s0 / sqrt(n0)), NA_real_)
p0 <- ifelse(is.finite(t0), 2 * pt(-abs(t0), df = n0 - 1), NA_real_)

m1 <- mean(aar1$ar_mm, na.rm = TRUE); s1 <- sd(aar1$ar_mm, na.rm = TRUE); n1 <- sum(is.finite(aar1$ar_mm))
t1 <- ifelse(n1 > 1 && s1 > 0, m1 / (s1 / sqrt(n1)), NA_real_)
p1 <- ifelse(is.finite(t1), 2 * pt(-abs(t1), df = n1 - 1), NA_real_)

cat("AAR day 0 =", round(100 * m0, 3), "%; t =", round(t0, 3),
    "; p =", signif(p0, 3), "; N =", n0, "\n")
cat("AAR day +1 =", round(100 * m1, 3), "%; t =", round(t1, 3),
    "; p =", signif(p1, 3), "; N =", n1, "\n")

# 3) Robustness checks

# (a) Market-adjusted model (AR = ret - mkt_ret)
df2$ar_ma <- df2$ret - df2$mkt_ret
ev_ma <- df2[df2$event_day %in% c(0, 1), ]
car_ma <- aggregate(ar_ma ~ stock_id, data = ev_ma, sum, na.rm = TRUE)
names(car_ma)[2] <- "CAR_ma"
car_ma <- car_ma[is.finite(car_ma$CAR_ma), ]

n_ma <- nrow(car_ma)
meanCAR_ma <- mean(car_ma$CAR_ma)
sdCAR_ma <- sd(car_ma$CAR_ma)
se_ma <- sdCAR_ma / sqrt(n_ma)
t_ma <- ifelse(se_ma > 0, meanCAR_ma / se_ma, NA_real_)
p_ma <- ifelse(is.finite(t_ma), 2 * pt(-abs(t_ma), df = n_ma - 1), NA_real_)

cat("Robustness (market-adjusted): Mean CAR[0,+1] =",
    round(100 * meanCAR_ma, 3), "%; t =", round(t_ma, 3),
    "; p =", signif(p_ma, 3), "; N =", n_ma, "\n")

# (b) Nonparametric signed-rank test (CAR from market model)
wt <- suppressWarnings(wilcox.test(car_mm$CAR_mm, mu = 0, alternative = "two.sided", conf.int = TRUE))
cat("Robustness (Wilcoxon signed-rank): W =", wt$statistic,
    "; p-value =", signif(wt$p.value, 3),
    "; median CAR[0,+1] estimate =", round(100 * wt$estimate, 3), "%\n")

# (c) Bootstrap CI for mean CAR (market model)
set.seed(123)
R <- 10000
boots <- replicate(R, mean(sample(car_mm$CAR_mm, size = n, replace = TRUE)))
ci <- quantile(boots, c(0.025, 0.975), na.rm = TRUE)
cat("Bootstrap 95% CI for mean CAR[0,+1] (market model): [",
    round(100 * ci[1], 3), "%,", round(100 * ci[2], 3), "% ]\n")
```

## 3. Expected Findings
- Sign: Negative. Sudden CEO deaths remove key managerial human capital and create transition risk; markets typically react adversely upon announcement.
- Magnitude: For a two-day window [0, +1], an average CAR around −1% to −2% is plausible, with day 0 carrying most of the impact and a smaller spillover into day +1. Robustness checks (market-adjusted model, signed-rank, bootstrap CI) should also indicate statistically significant negativity.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Event study — market model AR; estimation [−10,−2]; event window [0,+1]
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Firms experience significant negative CAR on CEO death announcement
